description: PRD-79: Unified Memory & Context Architecture — 5-layer memory stack (L0 Focus, L1 Working/Redis, L2 Short-term/Postgres, L3 Long-term/Mem0, L4 Org Knowledge), single UnifiedMemoryService replacing 12 scattered Mem0Client instances, Context Router for intelligent pre-LLM context assembly, and NL2SQL for live data queries.

userStories.title: Create UnifiedMemoryService singleton with shared Mem0Client
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a single entry point for all memory operations so that all consumers share one Mem0Client, one circuit breaker, and one connection pool.
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/modules/memory/unified_memory_service.py with UnifiedMemoryService class
Singleton pattern via classmethod get_instance() — returns same instance across all callers
Holds ONE shared Mem0Client instance (from integrations/mem0_client.py)
Holds ONE Redis client via get_redis_client()
DB sessions acquired per-request from async pool (NOT held as singleton state)

Exports MemoryNamespace helper that builds standardized user_id strings: mem:{workspace_id}, mem:{workspace_id}:agent:{agent_id}, mem:{workspace_id}:recipe:{recipe_id}, mem:{workspace_id}:daily, mem:session:{workspace_id}:{conversation_id}
Public async methods stubbed (empty, return None/empty list): store_long_term(), search_long_term(), get_all_memories(), delete_memory()
Module-level get_unified_memory_service() convenience function
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is the foundation — stubs only, no logic yet. The MemoryNamespace helper is critical for eliminating the 5+ user_id format inconsistencies. Import Mem0Client from modules.memory.integrations.mem0_client. Import get_redis_client from core.redis.client. Use typing for all method signatures.

search_long_term(workspace_id, query, agent_id=None, limit=5) delegates to Mem0Client.search() with correct namespace user_id
get_all_memories(workspace_id, agent_id=None) delegates to Mem0Client.get_all() with correct namespace user_id
delete_memory(memory_id) delegates to Mem0Client.delete()
All methods use MemoryNamespace to build user_ids — never raw string concatenation
All methods have try/except with logging (exc_info=True) and return empty results on failure
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This wraps the existing Mem0Client methods with the new namespace strategy. No new external dependencies.

userStories.title: Implement L1 Redis session store in UnifiedMemoryService
userStories.description: As a user, I want my conversation context to persist across browser refreshes within a 24-hour session so agents remember what we just discussed.
acceptanceCriteria: Add SessionMemory dataclass: summary (str), decisions (list[str]), action_items (list[str]), exchange_count (int), last_updated (datetime)
Add get_session(workspace_id, conversation_id) -> Optional[SessionMemory] — reads from Redis key mem:session:{workspace_id}:{conversation_id}, deserializes JSON

Add update_session(workspace_id, conversation_id, user_msg, assistant_msg) — appends exchange, updates summary (simple truncation to last 500 chars for now, not LLM summarization), increments exchange_count, writes to Redis with 24hr TTL
Add end_session(workspace_id, conversation_id) — marks session ended, sets TTL to 1hr (for consolidation window)
Redis key format: mem:session:{workspace_id}:{conversation_id}
All methods have try/except — Redis failures must never break chat

userStories.notes: This is greenfield — no existing Redis session store in the chat path. The summary is naive truncation for now (Phase 2 adds LLM rolling summary). Use json.dumps/loads for Redis serialization. 24hr TTL via redis.setex().

userStories.title: Add Redis caching layer for L3 Mem0 search results
userStories.description: As a system, I need to cache Mem0 search results in Redis to reduce cold-fetch latency from 200-500ms to <5ms for repeated queries.
acceptanceCriteria: In UnifiedMemoryService.search_long_term(), before calling Mem0Client.search(), check Redis cache
Cache key: mem:cache:{workspace_id}:{agent_id or 'global'}:{sha256(query)[:16]}
Cache TTL: 5 minutes (configurable via config.py constant MEMORY_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=300)
On cache hit: return deserialized results directly (skip Mem0)
On cache miss: call Mem0, cache the results, return them
Cache invalidation: in store_long_term(), delete all cache keys matching mem:cache:{workspace_id}:* pattern
Add MEMORY_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS to config.py
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use redis.setex() for TTL. For invalidation, use redis.delete() with a scan pattern — but be careful with KEYS command at scale. Consider using a Redis SET to track cache keys per workspace for targeted invalidation.

userStories.title: Create memory_short_term Postgres table and Alembic migration

Composite index on (workspace_id, created_at DESC) for time-range queries
Index on (workspace_id, decay_score) for decay job
Index on (workspace_id, promoted_to_l3) for promotion job
Migration runs successfully (upgrade and downgrade)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Follow existing migration patterns in alembic/versions/. Use UUID for id (import uuid, default=uuid.uuid4). workspace_id should reference workspaces table. agent_id references agents table.

userStories.title: Build Context Router with temporal detection and session hydration
userStories.description: As a system, I need an intelligent pre-LLM context assembly layer that decides what context to inject based on query analysis.
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/modules/memory/context_router.py with ContextRouter class

analyze_query(query: str) method returns ContextSignals dataclass with: is_temporal (bool), is_personal_fact (bool), is_session_continuation (bool), is_knowledge_query (bool), is_live_data (bool), temporal_window (Optional[tuple[datetime, datetime]])
Temporal detection uses regex patterns for: 'last week', 'yesterday', 'earlier today', 'last month', 'recently', date references, relative time phrases
Personal fact detection uses keyword patterns: 'my name', 'I prefer', 'I like', 'remember when', 'you told me'
Knowledge query detection: 'find the doc', 'what\'s our policy', 'search for', 'look up'
Live data detection: 'current', 'how many', 'latest', 'MRR', 'revenue', 'users signed up'
analyze_query() runs in <10ms (regex only, no LLM calls)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Keep this fast — regex patterns only, no NLP models. The temporal window calculation should convert 'last week' to (now-7d, now), 'yesterday' to (yesterday_start, yesterday_end), etc.

userStories.title: Implement Context Router retrieve_context() assembly method
userStories.description: As a system, I need the Context Router to assemble the right context bundle based on query signals.
acceptanceCriteria: Add retrieve_context(workspace_id, agent_id, query, conversation_id=None) to ContextRouter
Returns ContextBundle dataclass with: session_summary (str), long_term_memories (list), temporal_results (list), daily_logs (list), knowledge_awareness (str), total_tokens_estimate (int)
If session_continuation signal: fetch L1 session summary from Redis
If temporal signal: fetch L2 short-term with time filter
If personal_fact signal: search L3 long-term via Mem0
If knowledge_query or live_data signal: inject awareness text only (no pre-fetch)
Default (no signals): L3 top 5 memories + L1 session summary if exists
Total context budget configurable: default 4000 tokens (add CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS to config.py)
Each source has a sub-budget: session=500, long_term=800, temporal=600, daily=400, awareness=200
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use UnifiedMemoryService methods for all data fetching. The budget allocation truncates results to fit within token limits. Use a simple len(text)//4 token estimate.

userStories.title: Implement Ebbinghaus decay scoring background job
userStories.description: As a system, I need an hourly job that calculates retention scores for L2 short-term memories and archives expired items.
acceptanceCriteria: Add run_decay() method to UnifiedMemoryService
For each L2 item: retention = exp(-0.1 * hours_elapsed) * (1 + 0.5*importance + 0.1*min(access_count, 10))
Update decay_score column with calculated retention value
Items with decay_score < 0.3: soft-delete or mark as archived (add archived_at column if needed)
Process in batches of 100 rows per workspace to avoid long-running transactions
Log summary: X items decayed, Y items archived for workspace Z
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This runs as a background job (hourly). Use math.exp() for the decay formula. Process workspace by workspace. If archived_at column needed, add a small migration.

userStories.title: Implement L2 to L3 promotion pipeline
userStories.description: As a system, I need a daily job that promotes high-importance, frequently-accessed L2 memories to L3 long-term storage via Mem0 fact extraction.
acceptanceCriteria: Add promote_to_long_term() method to UnifiedMemoryService
Promotion criteria: importance > 0.7 AND access_count > 3 AND promoted_to_l3 = false
For each qualifying item: call Mem0Client.add() with infer=True (enables fact extraction and deduplication)
Mark promoted items: set promoted_to_l3=true, promoted_at=now()
Process in batches per workspace
Log summary: X items promoted for workspace Y
Add run_promotion() that iterates all workspaces (for scheduler)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The infer=True flag on Mem0 add() triggers LLM fact extraction — this is what makes L3 smart. Promoted items stay in L2 until decay removes them (belt and suspenders).

userStories.title: Wire session consolidation job (L1 to L2)
userStories.description: As a system, I need expired L1 sessions to be consolidated into L2 short-term storage so important decisions are preserved.
acceptanceCriteria: Add consolidate_session(workspace_id, conversation_id) method to UnifiedMemoryService
Reads the L1 Redis session, extracts key decisions and action items
Stores each decision/action item as separate L2 entries with content_type='session_decision' and importance=0.6
Deletes the L1 Redis key after successful consolidation
Add run_session_consolidation() that scans for sessions where end_session was called >1hr ago
Uses Redis SCAN (not KEYS) to find expired session keys matching mem:session:* pattern
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use SCAN instead of KEYS for production safety. The 1hr window gives the user time to resume before consolidation. Decisions and action items are extracted from the SessionMemory.decisions and SessionMemory.action_items fields.
